Agent Definition Reference ​

A custom agent is a directory. Its persona, its permissions, its skills, and the MCP servers it may reach are all files on disk under the agents root — nothing about an agent lives only in a database row. This page is the file format. The end-to-end walkthrough is in Writing a Custom Agent.

The agents root ​

The root is resolved per call, so it follows the tenant scope: SAIDI_AGENTS_DIR when set (tests), otherwise the current workspace's agents directory.

A directory becomes an agent when it contains an AGENT.md. A directory without one is skipped entirely — it is not listed, not spawnable, and not editable.

Directory names are validated as slugs before creation:

RuleValue
Length2–40 characters
Shape^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$ — lowercase letters, digits, dashes
Reservedprime, operator, saidi, plus any registered project name

On-disk layout ​

Every file an agent can have:

PathWritten byWhat it is
AGENT.mdyou / create_agentFrontmatter config + the persona prompt. Required
.claude-plugin/plugin.jsonscaffoldPlugin manifest — { name, description, version }
.codex-plugin/plugin.jsonyouSame manifest plus "skills": "./skills/"
mcp.jsonadd_mcp_serverMCP servers attached to this agent only
mcp-auth/<server>.jsonthe OAuth flowStored tokens for one url server. Never leaves disk
skills/<slug>/SKILL.mdadd_skill / import_skillOne skill: frontmatter + procedure
skills/<slug>/**import_skillA skill's own references/, scripts/, data files
workspace/the agentWorking directory when frontmatter sets cwd: workspace
anything elseyouReference assets the agent reads at run time

A real one, agents/content-creator/:

AGENT.md
mcp.json
mcp-auth/magnific.json
.claude-plugin/plugin.json
.codex-plugin/plugin.json
skills/content-creator-pro/SKILL.md
skills/content-creator-pro/_meta.json
skills/content-creator-pro/voice.md
skills/content-creator-pro/human_writing.md
skills/content-creator-pro/content_tracker.py
skills/magnific/SKILL.md
skills/magnific/references/image-generation.md
skills/magnific/references/video-generation.md

AGENT.md ​

The parser is deliberate and small, and it is not YAML. A frontmatter block must be the literal --- fence at the very start of the file. Inside it, each line is split on its first colon; the key is trimmed, the value is the raw rest of the line. There is no nesting, no list syntax, and no type coercion — tools is a comma-separated string, and lead is the text true or yes. Everything below the closing fence is the persona prompt.

KeyTypeDefaultEffect
descriptionstringfirst body line, # strippedHow PRIME routes to this agent; shown in list_agents
departmentstringtitle-cased directory nameGroups the agent with its team
leadtrue | yesabsent = falseGives the agent delegation tools over its department
cwdpaththe agent directoryWhere the agent runs
permissionall | read-only | customallWhat the agent may do
toolscomma-separated namesemptyExact allow-list, only meaningful with permission: custom
modelmodel idinheritModel override for this agent
profileprovider profile idinheritProvider profile this agent defaults to
efforteffort modeinheritDefault effort mode
hidden / enabledtrue/yes / false/noabsenthidden: true or enabled: false drops the agent from the roster fed to PRIME

cwd resolution: a leading ~ expands to the home directory, an absolute path is used as-is, and anything else resolves against the agent's own directory. agents/email uses cwd: workspace, so it runs in agents/email/workspace/. The directory is created on spawn if it does not exist.

A retired agent stays on disk when hidden — Settings still lists it and can restore or re-publish it — but it no longer occupies space in PRIME's prompt or dilutes routing.

markdown
---
description: Invoices, quotations, and client billing for First Click Technology Solutions.
department: Finance
cwd: /Users/said/Company/Invoices
lead: true
---

You are Said's Finance agent…

How permission is enforced ​

The permission is enforced by the tool set, not only by a callback. A model cannot call a tool it was never handed; the canUseTool gate is the second line of defence, and it matters because it also covers MCP tools, which tools does not govern.

permissionTool set handed to the runtimeGate
read-onlyexactly Read, Grep, Globread-only gate on the same three
customthe claude_code presetallow-list gate built from tools
allthe claude_code presetallow-all

Grep and Glob are named explicitly rather than assumed: native builds may route search through Bash, so a read-only agent without them would have no way to search at all.

mcp.json ​

Per-agent MCP servers live in mcp.json — the same shape as Claude's .mcp.json, but deliberately not named .mcp.json. The agent directory is already loaded as a local plugin, and the plugin loader would auto-connect a .mcp.json on its own. Saidi reads this file explicitly and hands the result to the runtime, so behaviour is identical across runtimes.

json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "magnific": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.magnific.com"
    }
  }
}

Two entry shapes are recognised. An entry with a url (and type other than stdio) is a remote server; otherwise a command is required and the entry is stdio.

FieldShapeNotes
typehttp | sse | stdioFor url entries, anything but sse normalizes to http
urlstringRequired for http/sse
headers{ string: string }Static headers merged with any OAuth header
commandstringRequired for stdio
argsstring[]Non-string members are dropped
env{ string: string }Passed on top of the default environment

Server names are validated on write: 2–40 characters, ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$, and saidi, saidi_mem, and saidi_dev are reserved for Saidi's own in-process servers. On read, an entry whose name fails validation or which normalizes to nothing is skipped — the file keeps it, the runtime does not see it. Attached servers are merged before Saidi's built-ins, so a built-in always wins a collision.

OAuth for remote servers ​

Only http/sse servers authenticate. The path is: probe → "needs auth" → authorize in the browser → tokens on disk → headers injected on every spawn.

Probe. Saidi connects to one configured server exactly the way a runtime would — an http config tries streamable HTTP and falls back to legacy SSE, an sse config tries SSE only, a stdio config spawns the command — lists its tools, then disconnects. The timeout is 10 seconds and tool listing follows at most 20 pages of cursor. The result is either the tool list or the reason it failed. A failure is reported as needsAuth when the error is an UnauthorizedError, carries code 401, or its message matches 401, unauthorized, or invalid_token. Probes only supply an auth provider when tokens already exist, so a bare 401 reads as "needs auth" rather than triggering a refresh dance against an unknown server.

Authorize. Starting auth registers a client with the server using this metadata:

json
{
  "client_name": "Saidi",
  "redirect_uris": ["http://127.0.0.1:4317/api/mcp/oauth/callback"],
  "grant_types": ["authorization_code", "refresh_token"],
  "response_types": ["code"],
  "token_endpoint_auth_method": "none"
}

The redirect URL is built from the configured host and port; a wildcard bind (0.0.0.0 or ::) is rewritten to 127.0.0.1 so the browser can actually reach it. If stored credentials are enough, the call returns authorized: true and nothing opens. Otherwise it returns the authorization URL for the UI to open, and the pending request — keyed by a random state id — is held for 10 minutes. The browser comes back to /api/mcp/oauth/callback, the code is exchanged, and the tokens are written.

Storage. One file per agent + server, agents/<name>/mcp-auth/<server>.json:

json
{
  "serverUrl": "https://mcp.magnific.com",
  "clientInformation": { "client_id": "…", "redirect_uris": ["…"], "scope": "…" },
  "tokens": { "access_token": "…", "refresh_token": "…", "token_type": "Bearer", "expires_in": 259200 },
  "obtainedAt": 1783266333672
}

Use. Every spawn reads the agent's servers with auth: for each server that has stored tokens, a fresh Authorization: Bearer … header is merged over the configured headers. A token within 60 seconds of expiry is refreshed first. If the refresh throws, the stale token is kept deliberately — the server will 401 and the MCP tab will show "needs auth", which is a better outcome than a hard failure inside the agent's next task.

mcp-auth/ is never packed into the agent's database document and is never pruned from disk. Those tokens exist in exactly one place.

Skills ​

Discovery. A skill is skills/<slug>/SKILL.md. The listing walks the skills/ directory, ignores any subdirectory without a SKILL.md, and reads name and description from the frontmatter (surrounding quotes are stripped, because real-world skills quote their values). A skill whose frontmatter fails to parse still lists, under its directory name.

Loading. The agent directory itself is handed to the runtime as a local plugin, with setting sources switched off entirely. That is what keeps an agent's skills, subagents, hooks, and configuration isolated from Saidi's own and from the user's global Claude configuration — the agent gets its home directory and nothing else.

Authoring. Writing a skill produces frontmatter with name and description (whitespace collapsed) followed by the body. The slug is validated the same way an agent name is, capped at 60 characters, and the resolved target must sit inside the agent's skills/ directory.

Importing. import_skill fetches from a URL and returns one of three results without touching disk:

ResultWhen
skillA SKILL.md was found — files are returned ready for review, plus the list of scripts among them
pagePlain text or HTML with no frontmatter — PRIME can author a SKILL.md from it
errorBinary content, a failed fetch, or no SKILL.md at the given location

A GitHub /tree/ URL is walked recursively through gh api (already authenticated, so private repos work) with the public REST API as fallback. A /blob/ URL, a raw URL, or any other page is fetched as a single file. The caps are boundaries, not suggestions:

CapValue
Files per skill50
Bytes per file256 KB
Bytes total1 MB
Page text kept20,000 characters
Fetch timeout30 s

SKILL.md must sit at the root of the folder you point at, or the import errors rather than guessing. Binary files are skipped with a note. Files counted as scripts are those under scripts/ or ending in .sh, .py, .js, .ts, .rb.

When the files are finally written, every relative path must resolve inside the skill directory — a single unsafe path refuses the entire import, because the remote repository chose those names.

Skills installed from the marketplace carry a _meta.json alongside SKILL.md recording owner, slug, version, and the upstream commit. See Marketplace.

The report contract ​

Every custom Claude agent and every project agent — in both ask and work mode — gets the report contract appended last in its system prompt, closest to the work. Its rules:

  • Ten lines or fewer by default; never more than twenty-five.
  • Open with the verdict — DONE, PARTIAL, or BLOCKED — then one line per thing asked.
  • Every claim carries its proof inline and nothing else: a file:line, a command and its exit code, a commit hash, or a count.
  • Never paste file contents, diffs, logs, test output, or code blocks. Cite the path.
  • The one exception: when a criterion asks for something to be in the report — a table, a list of states, a set of findings — that content is the deliverable and goes inline in full. Writing it to a file and citing the path does not satisfy it.
  • No narration. Only what is true now and how it can be checked.
  • Say ✗ plainly for anything not done, with the reason on one line.

The reasoning is economic: a final message is a handover into another model's context, and that context is replayed on every later turn. A long report is not paid for once. It is also self-defeating, because anything over the context budget is clipped before the reader sees it. The contract deliberately does not go to the verifier or the memory curator — both already have strict output formats of their own.

Three other fragments are appended to a custom agent's system prompt, in this order: the persona body, a workspace line naming the working directory, an execution-efficiency rule (batch independent read-only inspections, keep mutations sequential), an approval-integrity rule (never claim the user approved something unless the approval is quoted in the current task text), then the report contract.

Custom agents vs project agents ​

Both use the same spawn machinery, and both get the report contract. Everything else differs.

Custom agentProject agent
Defined byagents/<name>/AGENT.mdAn entry in the project registry
Rooted atcwd frontmatter, default the agent dirThe repository checkout
ConfigurationThe agent dir loaded as a local plugin; setting sources offThe repo's own .claude/ (project + local setting sources)
ModesOne mode; behaviour comes from the personaask (read-only Q&A) and work (make a change)
Permissionall / read-only / custom from frontmatterask is Read/Grep/Glob only; work gets the full preset
GitNoneCuts a saidi/* branch, commits, pushes, opens a PR — or commits on the current branch
MCPThe agent's own mcp.json, plus saidi_memsaidi_mem and whatever the repo configures
Memorymemory/agents/<name>.mdmemory/projects/<name>.md
Delegated byrun_agentdelegate_to_project
PolicyFrontmatterProject policy

Both inject their long-term memory block into the task text, not the system prompt — a remember save mid-run would otherwise change the system prompt and invalidate the resumed session's entire prompt cache. It is sent on a fresh session only, and re-sent after a context compaction.

Only forge is scaffolded automatically on a fresh install. Every other agent is something you or PRIME created.

Storage ​

The database is the source of truth for agent definitions; the directory tree is a materialized working copy that the runtimes load. Every mutation writes the agent's whole directory through to its document, best-effort — a failed persist never breaks the mutation — the materialized directory stays authoritative for the running agent.

Packing is bounded by construction. Files are taken smallest first against a 12 MB budget, so the definition itself — AGENT.md, plugin.json, skills/*/SKILL.md, mcp.json, all kilobytes — always fits, and only a fat tail of large files is reported as skipped and left on disk. Never packed at all: mcp-auth/ (secrets), workspace/ (run output), and node_modules at any depth. Anything excluded from the document is also preserved on disk by the pruner, because for those paths the disk is the only copy.

The shipped roster ​

The agents in this install, their departments, and what each owns:

AgentDepartmentOwns
companyCompany (lead)Company knowledge and operations — clients, contracts, proposals, HR, legal, project records. Runs from the company folder
content-creatorCreative (lead)Graphical content: social posts, banners, logos, mockups, slides, image edits. Attaches the magnific MCP server
corex-crmCommunicationThe Apex Aion CRM — reading records, creating and updating entries, pulling data. Attaches the corex-prod MCP server
emailCommunication (lead)Email search, drafting, sending, and inbox triage. Runs from its own workspace/; carries the himalaya skill
financeFinance (lead)Invoices, quotations, and client billing. Runs inside the real Invoices folder and matches its house format
forgeDevelopment (lead)Engineering lead: routes coding work to repo agents, and handles desktop/environment tasks itself (VPN, app runs, browser, screenshots)
tasksPersonal (lead)Personal task and thought organizer — captures brain-dumps, keeps a persistent list, reports what is on the plate

Departments and leads are covered in Agents & Departments.
